// Part: room: kitchen. Interior of the kitchen box x48..57 x z62..74, floor row y4 (the shell's floor is y3).
// Layout (x across, z down): the focal range (smoker, furnace, cauldron sink, barrel) on the east wall under the
// east window, a smooth_stone work counter along x56, a central work island x50..52 z68..69, a sink counter under
// the south windows, and barrels by the rear door. Lanes stay clear from the north openings (z61) to the rear door
// (x48 z75) and across the room to the west opening (x47). Light: three lanterns hung from chains under the ceiling
// (y10) plus the lit smoker and furnace.
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

const ORIGIN = [48, 4, 62]; // x48, floor row y4, z62; rows run along +z, columns along +x

// y4: floor-standing pieces
const Y4 = [
  ".........B", // z62: barrel in the north-east corner
  "........#S", // z63: counter, smoker on the east wall
  "........#F", // z64: counter, furnace
  "........#C", // z65: counter, cauldron sink under the east window
  "........#B", // z66: counter, barrel
  "..........", // z67
  ".L###....L", // z68: standing lanterns by the island (x49) and on the east wall (x57); island x50..52
  "..###.....", // z69
  "..........", // z70
  "..........", // z71
  "..........", // z72
  ".B..##....", // z73: barrel, sink counter under the south window (x54..55)
  ".L........", // z74: lantern in the south-west corner; x48 stays clear in front of the rear door
];
const LEGEND4 = {
  S: ["smoker", { facing: "west", lit: "true" }],
  F: ["furnace", { facing: "west", lit: "true" }],
  C: "cauldron",
  B: "barrel",
  "#": "smooth_stone",
  L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
};

// y5: things standing on the counter tops and island (standing lanterns sit on the counter and island blocks)
const Y5 = [
  "..........",
  "........f.", // z63: flower pot on the counter (herb pot)
  "........L.", // z64: standing lantern on the counter (lights the range and the sink)
  "........k.", // z65: lit candle on the sink counter
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..f.......", // z68: flower pot on the island
  "..L.k.....", // z69: standing lantern on the island (x50), lit candle (x52)
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
];
const LEGEND5 = {
  f: "flower_pot",
  k: ["candle", { candles: "3", lit: "true" }],
  L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
};

// y8 and y9: two hanging lanterns, each on an iron_chain from the ceiling (y10). One over the sink (x55 z64),
// one over the island (x51 z69). Lanterns hang at y8 under the chain cell at y9.
const Y8 = [
  "..........",
  "..........",
  ".......l..", // z64: lantern over the sink (x55)
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "...l......", // z69: lantern over the island (x51)
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
];
const Y9 = [
  "..........",
  "..........",
  ".......i..", // z64: chain up to the ceiling
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "...i......", // z69: chain
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
  "..........",
];

const LEGEND_HANG = {
  l: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }],
  i: ["iron_chain", { axis: "y" }],
};

export function build(g) {
  // one layers() call per y level; rows are 10 wide (x48..57), 13 deep (z62..74)
  layers(g, ORIGIN, LEGEND4, [Y4]);
  layers(g, [48, 5, 62], LEGEND5, [Y5]);
  layers(g, [48, 8, 62], LEGEND_HANG, [Y8]);
  layers(g, [48, 9, 62], LEGEND_HANG, [Y9]);
}

input.summary:
room: kitchen (parts/room-12.mjs) is laid out as written: smoker, furnace, cauldron sink, barrels, work island, lanterns and candles, 31 blocks. Built alone on a fresh grid it places all 31, all on palette.json.
In the full build all 31 writes are REFUSED: the shell air-fills the wing interior (shell.mjs box(37,61,58,75)), and runParts locks air too. The kitchen is not built, and room-12.mjs is unchanged.
Clearing the REFUSED line would mean deleting the kitchen, so I did not; the fix belongs to the shell or to runParts, not this file.
left: REFUSED 31 still open: every cell the kitchen uses (x48..57, z62..74, y4..9) is air that parts/shell.mjs:27 (box(37,61,58,75) fill 'air') already wrote, and runParts locks air as owned. No cell in the kitchen box is free, so moving writes cannot clear it. Only deleting them would, and that empties the room.

Decision needed outside room-12.mjs: either (a) shell.mjs stops air-filling room interiors (rooms are left unwritten by the shell and carved by their own parts), or (b) runParts lets a room part overwrite air an earlier part carved. (b) changes the library contract ('air included, so no carving'), so the owner should choose.
OFF-PALETTE: none for room-12. Every block (barrel, smoker, furnace, cauldron, flower_pot, candle, lantern, iron_chain, smooth_stone) is in palette.json, verified by building the part alone.
make.sh writes build.nbt, but the kitchen contributes no blocks to it until the lock is resolved.

waste.what: Working out why all 31 writes were refused: I read shell.mjs and runParts by hand to find that every refusal was the shell's air fill, not a per-cell conflict. The parts report only lists the first 8 refusals and does not name the owner.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and roughly 150 lines of source read
waste.tool: runParts report should group refusals by owning part and call (e.g. 'owned by shell.mjs box() air fill: 31 of 31 writes'), and print a one-line 'air-filled interior' warning when a room part's whole footprint is already owned.

waste.what: Checking whether the part's own content was valid (layout, palette) while the lock blocked it. I wrote a scratch script that builds room-12 alone on a fresh grid, then deleted it.
waste.cost: 1 scratch script and 2 runs; the lock hid the palette result in the real build
waste.tool: A way to build one part on its own, e.g. `make.sh --only 'room: kitchen'` or an `alone: true` option on runParts, reporting placed, off-palette and refused counts.

waste.what: OFF-PALETTE is not reported for a part whose writes are refused, because the lock check returns before the palette check. A part with both problems shows only the REFUSED line, so a fix for the lock would expose off-palette blocks one run later.
waste.cost: one extra make.sh cycle, and it can only be found by hand
waste.tool: runParts should run the palette check before the lock check, so both problems show in one run.

companions.task: Decide whether the mansion shell should leave room interiors unwritten, or whether room parts may overwrite air the shell carved. Either choice changes the shell or the runParts contract, so it is not a room-12 edit.
